prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: high-resolution transparent source-pose sprite page for Skeleton animation.
Generate newly drawn art, not enlarged original pixels. Layout FOUR columns by TWO rows in exact row-major order, wide 2:1 canvas. Each occupied cell is one complete source pose (or its source death fragments). Keep generous truly transparent gutters and outer margins: whole body, sword, fingers and toes fit in central 75 percent of each cell. Distinct figures must remain spatially separate, no overlaps. Do not add labels or grid.
Input image 1 is APPROVED APPEARANCE ONLY: unarmored human skeleton with warm aged ivory bone, fine cracks, olive-brown patina, hollow dark eye sockets, finely modeled volume. Same lean proportions and exposed ribs/pelvis, bare bony hands and feet. One straight double-edged steel sword, brass/gold crossguard and pommel, dark violet grip. No shield, armor, cloth, glow or new props.
Input image 2 is ORIGINAL POSE AUTHORITY. Follow each guide cell's exact camera/view, shoulder/pelvis turn, skull tilt, joint/foot placement and sword-hand grip, not the master's idle stance. Keep subtle pose differences, do not repeat an idle to fill cells. Original near anatomical sword arm is the hand on screen-left in frontal view; do not swap it when torso rotates. Preserve all source views even when away from camera, and source disarticulation/death fragments. Exactly ONE sword per occupied pose, held by source hand unless the source releases it.

Exact requested mapping (prefix every numbered pose below with skeleton_). Match the corresponding guide cell exactly:
Cell 1: p024: defensive rise, torso upright, original near sword fist brought forward to waist, blade diagonal upper RIGHT about35 degrees, free hand open in front to right; forward knee raised.
Cell 2: p025: defensive high guard, thin right side/three-quarter view, original sword hand before chest, blade steeper upper RIGHT, empty hand open beside it without changing grip; front knee lifted.
Cell 3: p026: defensive peak, original sword hand near abdomen and blade almost VERTICAL above skull, torso drawn back/right-side view, knees bent, one foot raised behind; preserve narrow foreshortened guard.
Cell 4: p027: DEATH frame0, right-facing startled backward lean, both arms thrown FORWARD, original near sword hand forward chest height and blade near-horizontal RIGHT seen dark/edge-on; legs bend and lift as guide. Not an attack pose.
Cell 5: p028: DEATH frame1, torso pulled back with both arms reaching up/forward toward upper right, sword hand retains hilt and blade slants upper RIGHT, head tipped back, both legs folded and feet lowering under body.
Cell 6: p029: DEATH frame2, body descending into kneeling collapse, two arms lifted above skull and sword almost vertical/slanting upper LEFT from held hilt, head tilted upward; source limbs compressed, not standing.
Cell 7: p030: DEATH frame3, kneeling collapsing skeleton with dislocating shoulder/arm bones and a small detached fragment above right shoulder; ONE sword has been RELEASED and floats above the figure, near-horizontal diagonal upper left, hilt toward right. Preserve fragment positions and source silhouette, no extra sword in hand.
Cell 8: p031: DEATH frame4, low crumpled disarticulating skeleton with bent legs/bone heap under body, skull above heap, some arm bones lifted; ONE sword descends near-vertically through/along heap, brass hilt near top. Preserve skeleton collapse and native detached fragments, no standing full body and no ground.
Background MUST be genuine transparent alpha, including holes between ribs and limbs. No haze, gradient, checkerboard, backdrop, floor, cast/contact shadows, text, labels, frames, grid, extra magic or motion trails. Every blade tip and bone inside canvas, no clipped components. Keep modeled bone/metal material finish consistent with approved master, but source pose and view take priority. Render at high resolution with fine shading rather than pixel clusters.
